blocks.prompt: 10. If \(x = \ln t\) and \(y = \frac{1}{t}\), show that \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - y = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Phir parametric equations; saabit karna hai ke second derivative wapas \(y\) ke barabar hai.
Diya kya hai? \(x = \ln t\), \(y = \frac{1}{t}\).
Saabit kya karna hai? \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - y = 0\).
Rule kaunsa? Parametric differentiation do dafa.
Plan: \(y_{1}\), phir \(y_{2}\), aur aakhir mein \(\frac{1}{t}\) ko \(y\) pehchanna.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x = \ln t\), \(y = \frac{1}{t}\) (\(t > 0\), kyunke \(\ln t\) sirf positive \(t\) ke liye hai).
Saabit karna: \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - y = 0\).
Tareeqa: parametric differentiation do dafa.

\(t\) ke lehaz se derivatives
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{t}, \quad \dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\ln t\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{t}\); \(\frac{1}{t} = t^{-1}\) ka derivative \(-t^{-2}\).

Pehla derivative
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-1/t^{2}}{1/t} = -\dfrac{1}{t}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}\); fraction ko fraction se divide karne par \(-\frac{1}{t^{2}} \times t = -\frac{1}{t}\).

Doosra derivative
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(-\dfrac{1}{t}\right)\cdot\dfrac{dt}{dx}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{t^{2}}\cdot t = \dfrac{1}{t} = y\]
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} - y = 0\]
Kyun: \(-t^{-1}\) ka derivative \(+t^{-2}\), aur \(\frac{dt}{dx} = \frac{1}{1/t} = t\). Bacha \(\frac{1}{t}\), jo diya hua \(y\) hi hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{dt}{dx}\) se multiply karna na bhoolein; warna jawab \(\frac{1}{t^{2}}\) aayega jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq
\(x = \ln t\) se \(t = e^{x}\), to \(y = e^{-x}\). Is ka har doosra derivative wapas \(e^{-x}\) hai, yani \(y_{2} = y\). Seedha bhi wohi.
